properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-18 for Mission Bay's second real-site pass: real, address-tagged OpenStreetMap building footprint for Madrone, a two-tower Bosa Development luxury condominium complex (329-330 units per secondary sources, opened 2011-2012, architect Perkins & Will per secondary sources) sharing Assessor Block 8720 with its sister project Radiance. Point-in-polygon checked against DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' layer (m288-24sn): this site falls in Mission Bay South, not Mission Bay North as this project's own brief informally grouped it -- corrected here against the authoritative boundary rather than the brief's casual wording. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the parenthetical above is corrected: (1) '329-330 units per secondary sources' is withdrawn, since Bosa's page gives 693 units for Radiance, Madrone and Arden combined and nothing cited gives Madrone's own count; (2) 'opened 2011-2012' is overstated, since Bosa says only that Madrone's two connected 16-storey towers were completed 'a few years' after 2008, while the DataSF Assessor roll gives year_property_built 2012 for the per-unit lots at 420 and 480 Mission Bay Blvd N and 435 China Basin St and SocketSite (July 29, 2010) reported Radiance West move-in expected by mid-2012; (3) 'architect Perkins & Will per secondary sources' is withdrawn: no cited source names an architect; (4) the OSM tag is name=, not addr:housename= (the digitized_from field is fixed). 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint(s), not a hand trace or plan estimate. The underlying Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across many individually owned per-unit lots (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson), so no single blklot represents the whole building and it cannot be joined via status.csv the way a single-owner parcel can. Using the real building footprint from OSM instead of a fabricated or arbitrarily chosen 'representative' unit lot, the same real-geometry-without-a-single-parcel pattern already used for several Pier 70 buildings (DataSF Building Footprints) and for Mission Bay's own real park polygons.'. REPLACED 2026-10-12 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner approved building records whose outline matches an Assessor lot at 85% or better, both ways, using the lot (CLAUDE.md, 'An official parcel beats our drawing'). DataSF's Assessor layer (data/raw/parcels.geojson) has Assessor lot 8720117 (11,410 m2, active, mapped 2012-06-20); the earlier outline of 10,169 m2 and the lot overlap with IoU 0.87 (99% of the earlier outline lies inside the lot and it covers 88% of the lot). The outline is now that lot using the lots' own vertices (no simplification). The lot is condominium-mapped: 332 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8720117 and 331 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. geometry_type stays 'real'. Previous accuracy_caveat: 'REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint(s), not a hand trace or plan estimate. The underlying Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across many individually owned per-unit lots (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data), so no single blklot represents the whole building and it cannot be mapped from one parcel the way a single-owner building can. Using the real building footprint from OSM instead of a fabricated or arbitrarily chosen 'representative' unit lot, the same real-geometry-without-a-single-parcel pattern already used for several Pier 70 buildings (DataSF Building Footprints) and for Mission Bay's own real park polygons.'. 2026-10-12 accuracy audit follow-up: the 2026-09-29 note above cites SocketSite (July 29, 2010) for a move-in expected by mid-2012. That post, 'Radiance West (325 China Basin Phase Two) Construction Underway', is about Radiance's Phase Two and says 'construction on the first 170 units of Radiance West (aka Radiance Phase Two of Three) has now begun in earnest and the units should be ready for move-in by mid-2012'. SocketSite's Madrone tag page links the two names ('Madrone: T-Minus Two Months to Official Grand Opening', June 29, 2011: 'a development born Radiance West but since dubbed “Madrone,”'), so the post bears on this building, but what it gives is an expected move-in date written in 2010, not an event, and it is not evidence of when Madrone opened. The Assessor's year built 2012 is a roll year, not a completion event. Bosa's page ('Radiance was the first major condominium development in the United States following the market downturn in 2008. A few years later, the two connected 16-storey towers of Madrone were completed') gives no year for either building: its '2008' is the market downturn, not a Radiance completion year. No source read gives Madrone's opening or completion date. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8720117 (11,410 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. The lot is condominium-mapped: 332 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8720117 and 331 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (OpenStreetMap (way 142845124, name=Madrone Mission Bay, 480 Mission Bay Blvd N)); 99% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 88% of the lot.
properties.notes: Unit count and opening year are not established by any cited source: Bosa's project page gives 693 units for Radiance, Madrone and Arden combined and says only that Radiance was the first major condominium development in the United States following the 2008 market downturn and that 'a few years later' Madrone's two connected 16-storey towers were completed (no year given); the Assessor roll gives year built 2012 (a roll year, not a completion event) for the condominium lots at 420 and 480 Mission Bay Blvd N and 435 China Basin St; and SocketSite (July 29, 2010) gave an expected move-in of mid-2012 for Radiance West, the name it later said had become Madrone (an expected date, not an opening).
